# 11QMelchizedek Column 2 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in 11QMelchizedek Column 2 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 2:1 — "shnat ha-yovel" — rendering of "jubilee year"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "year-of-the-jubilee" | Hyphenated construct chain preserving Hebrew syntax |
| LOGOS | "year of jubilee" | Standard formal English rendering |
| PNEUMA | "jubilee year" | Natural English word order for modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "year of jubilee." This preserves the biblical phrasing familiar from Leviticus 25 without the mechanical hyphenation of EMET or the inversion of PNEUMA.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:2 — "ba'al masheh yado" — rendering of the creditor phrase

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "possessor-of-a-loan-of his-hand" | Ultra-literal rendering of the Hebrew idiom |
| LOGOS | "creditor" | Standard formal equivalent per Deut 15:2 |
| PNEUMA | "creditor" | Same as LOGOS; natural English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/PNEUMA rendering "creditor." EMET's hyper-literal rendering obscures the meaning of a standard biblical idiom that has a well-established English equivalent.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 2:3 — "shemittah la-El" — "release of God" vs. "God's release"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the release of-God" | Literal construct with hyphen |
| LOGOS | "the release of God" | Formal construct without hyphen |
| PNEUMA | "God's release" | Possessive form for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "the release of God." Matches the Deuteronomy 15:2 phrasing in standard English translations. PNEUMA's possessive is acceptable but less traditional.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:5 — "pesher" formula — "Its interpretation" vs. "This means"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Its interpretation" | Literal rendering of pesher |
| LOGOS | "Its interpretation" | Formal equivalent, standard scholarly rendering |
| PNEUMA | "This means" | Dynamic rendering for accessibility |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS rendering "Its interpretation." The pesher formula is a technical genre marker that should be preserved; "this means" loses the exegetical specificity.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:5 — "bene shamayim" — "Sons of Heaven"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-Sons-of-Heaven" | Hyphenated literal form |
| LOGOS | "the Sons of Heaven" | Formal rendering preserving title |
| PNEUMA | "the Sons of Heaven" | Same; recognized as a fixed title |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/PNEUMA rendering "the Sons of Heaven." All three agree on preserving this as a sectarian title; EMET's hyphenation is unnecessary for a proper designation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 2:6 — "chovat" — "debt" vs. "burden"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-debt-of" | Literal rendering connecting to jubilee/release language |
| LOGOS | "the debt of" | Formal rendering maintaining financial metaphor |
| PNEUMA | "the burden of" | Dynamic rendering emphasizing oppressive weight of sin |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS rendering "the debt of." The jubilee context makes the financial metaphor (debt-release) theologically significant; "burden" loses this crucial thematic connection.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:6 — "'avonot" — "iniquities" vs. "sins"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their-iniquities" | Literal; 'avon specifically means iniquity/guilt |
| LOGOS | "their iniquities" | Formal equivalent preserving the specific Hebrew term |
| PNEUMA | "their sins" | Dynamic; more accessible English equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS rendering "their iniquities." The Hebrew 'avon carries a specific weight of guilt and moral crookedness distinct from the generic chata' ("sin").

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:7 — "[happen]" vs. "[take place]" vs. "[come about]"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "will [happen]" | Simple literal reconstruction |
| LOGOS | "will [take place]" | Formal register |
| PNEUMA | "will [come about]" | Dynamic phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "will [take place]." Slightly more formal and appropriate to the eschatological register of the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:9 — "anshe goral Melchizedek" — "men of the lot" vs. "people of the lot" vs. "people who belong to"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-men-of the-lot-of" | Literal with construct-chain hyphenation |
| LOGOS | "the men of the lot of" | Formal rendering preserving "lot" (goral) |
| PNEUMA | "the people who belong to" | Dynamic rendering explaining the "lot" metaphor |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted compromise "the people of the lot of." Uses inclusive "people" (from PNEUMA) while preserving the technical "lot" (goral) terminology (from EMET/LOGOS) that is central to Qumran dualism.

**Status:** Resolved as compromise.

---

## 2:11 — "shenat ratson" — "year of favor" vs. "year of grace"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-year-of-favor" | Literal rendering of ratson |
| LOGOS | "the year of favor" | Standard rendering per Isa 61:2 ("year of the LORD's favor") |
| PNEUMA | "the year of grace" | Dynamic rendering emphasizing divine mercy |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS rendering "the year of favor." This matches the standard English of Isaiah 61:2 and preserves the specific Hebrew ratson (= favor, acceptance, goodwill), which is distinct from chen (= grace).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:13 — "shirei David" — "songs of David" vs. "psalms of David"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-songs-of-David" | Literal rendering of shirei |
| LOGOS | "the psalms of David" | Standard formal term for the Davidic collection |
| PNEUMA | "the psalms of David" | Same; universally recognized designation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/PNEUMA rendering "the psalms of David." While EMET's "songs" is technically accurate for shirei, the context clearly refers to the biblical Psalter, and "psalms" is the expected English designation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 2:14 — "elohim" (plural, council members) — "the gods" vs. "the divine beings" vs. "the divine beings"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the gods" | Ultra-literal rendering of elohim as plural noun |
| LOGOS | "the divine beings" | Formal rendering distinguishing from God Most High |
| PNEUMA | "the divine beings" | Dynamic rendering; same conclusion as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/PNEUMA rendering "the divine beings." While EMET's "the gods" is technically literal, "divine beings" better conveys the Second Temple understanding of the heavenly council without implying polytheism.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 2:15 — "al marom El yashpot" — rendering of Ps 7:8–9 application

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "and-on-high God will-[j]udge the-peoples" | Literal with "God" for El |
| LOGOS | "and God on high will [j]udge the peoples" | Formal; repositions "on high" for English flow |
| PNEUMA | "God above will [j]udge the nations" | Dynamic; "above" for marom, "nations" for 'ammim |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "and God on high will [j]udge the peoples." Better English syntax than EMET while preserving "peoples" (not "nations") for 'ammim. PNEUMA's "nations" slightly overtranslates.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:20 — "niqmat mishpetei El" — "vengeance of the judgments of God"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-veng[eance]-of the-judgments-of-God" | Literal double-construct chain |
| LOGOS | "the veng[eance] of the judgments of God" | Formal rendering preserving both nouns |
| PNEUMA | "God's veng[eance] and judgment" | Dynamic; simplifies the construct chain |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS rendering "the veng[eance] of the judgments of God." The double construct is theologically precise — this is not simply "vengeance and judgment" but vengeance that consists in executing God's judgments. PNEUMA's simplification loses this.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:21 — "elim" — "gods" vs. "divine beings" vs. "heavenly beings"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-[eternal] gods" | Literal rendering of elim |
| LOGOS | "the [eternal] divine beings" | Formal rendering consistent with 2:14 |
| PNEUMA | "the [eternal] heavenly beings" | Dynamic; specifies the cosmic location |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "the [eternal] divine beings." Maintains consistency with the rendering of elohim in 2:14. PNEUMA's "heavenly" adds interpretive specificity not in the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:22 — "davar" — "affair" vs. "affair" vs. "mission"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-[a]ffair-of-Melchizedek" | Literal rendering of davar |
| LOGOS | "the [a]ffair of Melchizedek" | Formal rendering preserving ambiguity of davar |
| PNEUMA | "the [m]ission of Melchizedek" | Dynamic; interprets davar as Melchizedek's eschatological task |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS rendering "the [a]ffair of Melchizedek." The Hebrew davar is deliberately ambiguous (word, matter, affair, thing); PNEUMA's "mission" imposes too specific an interpretation on a fragmentary context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:24 — "malakh Elohayikh" — "Your God reigns" vs. "Your God is king"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Your-God [reigns]" | Literal rendering of malakh as "reigns" |
| LOGOS | "Your God [reigns]" | Standard rendering per Isa 52:7 |
| PNEUMA | "Your God [is king]" | Dynamic; emphasizes the royal title |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS rendering "Your God [reigns]." This matches the standard English rendering of Isaiah 52:7 and preserves the verbal form (malakh = "has become king / reigns").

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:25 — pesher formula variation — "Its interpretation" vs. "This means"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Its interpretation" | Consistent pesher formula |
| LOGOS | "Its interpretation" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "This means" | Dynamic equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS rendering "Its interpretation." Consistency with 2:5 and the pesher genre requires preserving the formula.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:26 — "mashiach nagid" — "an anointed one, a prince" vs. "an anointed ruler"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "an-anointed-one, a-prince" | Two-term rendering preserving both Hebrew nouns |
| LOGOS | "an anointed one, a prince" | Formal rendering preserving apposition |
| PNEUMA | "an anointed ruler" | Dynamic; combines into single phrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS rendering "an anointed one, a prince." Daniel 9:25's mashiach nagid uses apposition — two distinct titles — which PNEUMA's compression into "anointed ruler" collapses.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements: 19*
*Resolution: LOGOS 7, EMET/LOGOS 7, LOGOS/PNEUMA 2, EMET/LOGOS/PNEUMA (against EMET hyphenation only) 1, Compromise 1, PNEUMA 0, EMET 1*
